messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — high error rate detected in apac1a affecting the edge path. 5xx surge from several customer-facing ALBs. Initial error rate spike at 12:03 UTC. Paging SRE oncall. :rotating_light:

sre-anna: seeing 5xx spike across multiple routes, primarily via apac1a-alb-01 -> ingress-nginx. lots of TLS handshakes queued, slow accepts.

net-eng-lee: confirmed abnormal backlog on ALB listeners in apac1a. Cloud metrics show listener_concurrent_handshakes >> baseline.

infra-jorge: any recent deploys to ingress?

sre-anna: not from us, last ingress-controller image was yesterday. k8s nodes seem healthy but pods reporting increased connection timeouts.

pd-support-ram: customers reporting intermittent 503/502; ticket flood in support queue. ETA to customer notifications?

customer-success-kai: sending proactive note to impacted tenants now. marking as partial outage for apac region.

sre-anna: quick checks:
```
kubectl -n ingress get pods -o wide
# pod logs show repeated TLS accept timeout errors from the controller
kubectl -n ingress logs ingress-nginx-0 | grep -i "accept" | tail -n 50
```

net-eng-lee: ALB target health shows lots of targets in draining/unused but not failing healthchecks fast enough. It looks like the ALB listener threadpool is saturated causing slow backend drains.

infra-jorge: grabbing control plane metrics from cloud console — CPU for the ALB control plane looks normal, but `ListenerSSLHandshakeTime` p50/p95 increased 10x.

sre-anna: mitigation plan attempt 1: scale ingress controller replicas + rotate one ALB target group out to force fresh TCP accepts. Doing quick scale now.

sre-anna: running:
```
kubectl -n ingress scale deploy ingress-nginx --replicas=6
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --targets Id=i-abc123 --region ap-southeast-2
```

net-eng-lee: hold on deregister, if we pull too many targets at once Route53 weight policies may trigger failover. We need gradual drain to avoid cross-region weight shift.

sre-anna: ack, will drain 1 at a time.

oncall-night-tim: I'm taking handoff for the next 2 hours. Ping me for any changes.

pd-support-ram: customers want ETA. Suggest message: "We're investigating elevated 5xx rates in APAC. Targeted mitigation underway, we'll update in 30m or sooner." Approve?

customer-success-kai: sending that now. include note about partial routing to fallback region if we need it.

infra-jorge: small update — Cloud provider reports a control plane alert around TLS hardware offload for some ALB hosts in apac1a. They're examining a firmware/driver interaction.

net-eng-lee: that matches the handshake backlog. If hardware offload is flapping, listeners would stall but targets remain registered -> backlog grows.

sre-anna: mitigation attempt 2: adjust ALB idle_timeout and reduce max_handshake_queue via CLI to force faster rejects and permit failover of traffic to healthy targets. Applying conservative changes.

sre-anna: command run:
```
aws elbv2 modify-load-balancer-attributes --load-balancer-arn arn:aws:... --attributes Key=idle_timeout.timeout_seconds,Value=15
# and set listener-level accept queue smaller (provider-specific flag)
```

net-eng-lee: provider flag applied, but control plane still shows occasional host-level stalls. Recommendation: shift 30% of traffic to apac1b via weighted DNS to reduce pressure and give provider time to remediate.

sre-anna: starting weighted DNS shift: Route53 change in progress — shifting 30% to apac1b.

incident-bot: DNS change applied by net-eng-lee at 12:26 UTC (change id: Z3ABC-CHANGE-789). TTL for record is 60s.

pd-support-ram: support queue volume dropping slightly. some customers still seeing errors, but rate halved.

customer-success-kai: sent follow-up note: "We've shifted some traffic to a healthy APAC zone and are monitoring. We'll update again in 20 minutes." :thumbsup:

oncall-night-tim: monitoring logs — envoy upstream 502s reduced but still present for long-tail requests >10s. Might need to increase backend connection pool size.

infra-jorge: vendor confirmed firmware bug affecting TLS offload on a subset of LB hosts. They propose either rolling hosts or disabling hardware offload on impacted hosts. Rolling could take 20-30m per host.

net-eng-lee: preference to disable hardware offload for affected hosts first to avoid full host roll. Applying change now.

infra-jorge: executed provider API to disable offload on 4 hosts. Control plane telemetry shows improved handshake latency within 5 minutes.

sre-anna: continuing to drain and re-register targets slowly to rebalance.

sre-anna: current status: 5xx spike reduced to baseline+10%. Edge path still showing minor errors for longer requests. Route53 shift holding steady at 30% apac1b.

pd-support-ram: triage summary for customers: partial impact for APAC small percentage of requests had 502/503 between 12:03-13:00 UTC, mitigations applied (scaled ingress, DNS weight shift, disabled TLS offload), provider now performing host patches.

customer-success-kai: creating a post-incident communication draft and sending to legal for review.

net-eng-lee: recommended follow-ups: 1) increase ALB listener telemetry retention, 2) add healthcheck for listener handshake latency to auto-fence hosts, 3) lower Route53 weigh-change TTL during incidents to speed failover, 4) run chaos test for TLS offload regressions.

sre-anna: taking action items: will file runbook updates and postmortem. Handing off to oncall-night-tim for monitoring and cleanup.

oncall-night-tim: acknowledged, I'm on watch. If 5xx returns >10% for >5m escalate to SRE lead and open priority with provider.

incident-bot: Incident state changed to mitigated at 13:01 UTC (incident id: INC-3265).

sre-anna: final note — the quick DNS weight shift was key to reducing blast radius without a full region failover. Will capture metrics for cost/latency tradeoffs in the postmortem.

customer-success-kai: logging customer messages sent and ticket IDs in the incident doc.

pd-support-ram: closing support triage, will attach logs to the incident doc.

sre-anna: thanks team. Postmortem owner assigned to me. I'll publish a first-draft within 24h.
